phrases.ar: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺
phrases.explanation: "To Allah alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And to Allah all matters will be returned for judgment." Everything in the heavens and on earth belongs to Allah, and all affairs return to Him for judgment on the Day of Resurrection. The grammarians differed over why the Name of Allah is repeated in "and to Allah the matters return," and the meaning is emphasis: all matters, great and small, return to Allah alone, and He will judge between His servants with justice. So turn to Him and ask Him, for He owns all things and to Him is the return.

phrases.ar: كُنتُمۡ خَيۡرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخۡرِجَتۡ لِلنَّاسِ تَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَتَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ
phrases.translation: You are the best community ever raised for humanity—you encourage good, forbid evil, and believe in Allah.
phrases.explanation: "You are the best community ever raised for humanity, you encourage good, forbid evil, and believe in Allah." You, O community of Muhammad, are the best nation brought forth for mankind, because you enjoin the good, forbid the evil, and believe in Allah. The exegetes differed over the details of this praise, some saying it is because of the enjoining of good and forbidding of evil, which is the noblest of deeds, and others adding the belief in Allah that completes it. This nation was sent as a mercy to all people, calling to the truth and forbidding falsehood. The exegetes said the best nation is the one that enjoins good and forbids evil, for that is the mission of the prophets, and your Prophet is the seal of them, sent to all mankind as a mercy, so hold fast to his way. Allah praised this nation because it combines faith, enjoining good, and forbidding evil, and no nation before it combined all of these as yours does. This is a praise of the nation that follows the Messenger, and a spur to hold fast to its Book and his Sunna. The reason for this superiority is that this nation was sent to all mankind, not to one people, and it calls to the oneness of Allah and to justice among people, so it is the best nation in the sight of Allah for what it enjoins and forbids and believes.

phrases.ar: ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَتُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ ءَامَنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَكَانَ خَيۡرٗا لَّهُمۚ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَأَكۡثَرُهُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
phrases.translation: Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them. Some of them are faithful, but most are rebellious
phrases.explanation: "Had the People of the Book believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are rebellious." If the People of the Book had believed in Muhammad and the Quran, it would have been better for them than their disbelief, for faith is the cause of success in this life and the next. Among them are some who believe, but most of them are rebellious, departing from the truth and their books, and they will be recompensed for it. So the People of the Book are urged to believe, for belief is better for them than disbelief. Among the People of the Book are the believers who will be saved, but most are fasiqun.

phrases.ar: لَن يَضُرُّوكُمۡ إِلَّآ أَذٗىۖ وَإِن يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ يُوَلُّوكُمُ ٱلۡأَدۡبَارَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
phrases.translation: They can never inflict harm on you, except a little annoyance. But if they meet you in battle, they will flee and they will have no helpers
phrases.explanation: "They can never inflict harm on you, except a little annoyance. But if they meet you in battle, they will flee and they will have no helpers." Allah consoles His Prophet and the believers: the People of the Book cannot truly harm you except a small annoyance, for Allah protects the believers. "Except harm" is a disconnected exception. And if they fight you, they will turn their backs and flee, and they will have no helpers against Allah, for He aids His party and humiliates His enemies, and whoever Allah humiliates has no helper. So do not fear them, for Allah is with the believers. And if they fight you, their flight is certain, for Allah does not aid the disbelievers.

phrases.ar: ضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ أَيۡنَ مَا ثُقِفُوٓاْ إِلَّا بِحَبۡلٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَحَبۡلٖ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡمَسۡكَنَةُۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلۡأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
phrases.translation: They will be stricken with disgrace wherever they go, unless they are protected by a covenant with Allah or a treaty with the people. They have invited the displeasure of Allah and have been branded with misery for rejecting Allah’s revelations and murdering ˹His˺ prophets unjustly. This is ˹a fair reward˺ for their disobedience and violations
phrases.explanation: "They will be stricken with disgrace wherever they go, unless they are protected by a covenant with Allah or a treaty with the people. They have drawn upon themselves Allah's displeasure by denying His signs. That is because they disbelieved in Allah's revelations and killed the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and transgressed." "Wherever they are found" means wherever they are encountered, humiliation is struck upon them, unless they hold fast to a covenant from Allah, which is Islam, or a treaty with the people, which is the jizya and the protection pact. They incurred the anger of Allah because they denied His signs and killed the prophets unjustly, and that is because they disobeyed Allah and transgressed His limits, and the recompense of the wrongdoer is humiliation and anger.

phrases.ar: ۞ لَيۡسُواْ سَوَآءٗۗ مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أُمَّةٞ قَآئِمَةٞ يَتۡلُونَ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَهُمۡ يَسۡجُدُونَ
phrases.translation: Yet they are not all alike: there are some among the People of the Book who are upright, who recite Allah’s revelations throughout the night, prostrating ˹in prayer˺
phrases.explanation: "Yet they are not all alike: there are some among the People of the Book who are upright, who recite Allah's revelations throughout the night, prostrating." "Not all alike": the People of the Book are not all the same, for among them is an upright community that recites the verses of Allah in the watches of the night and prostrates in prayer, believing in Allah and the Last Day, enjoining good and forbidding evil. These are the righteous of them, and they are not like the majority who are rebellious. They stand in prayer at night, reciting the Quran, and they are an example for the believers.

phrases.ar: يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَيَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَيَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَيُسَٰرِعُونَ فِي ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
phrases.translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, encourage good and forbid evil, and race with one another in doing good. They are ˹truly˺ among the righteous
phrases.explanation: "They believe in Allah and the Last Day, encourage good and forbid evil, and race with one another in doing good. They are truly among the righteous." "An upright community": a nation standing upon the truth, in the nominative because of "among the People of the Book." They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin the good, forbid the evil, and hasten to do good deeds, competing in charity and righteousness. They are among the righteous, and Allah will reward them for their faith and their deeds, for He does not waste the reward of the doers of good. These three verses were revealed, it is mentioned, concerning a group of the Jews who believed, and others said the comparison is between the People of the Book and the community of Muhammad, which is upright in the right of Allah, and the two are not alike in reward. "An upright community" means a group standing upon the truth, and the exegetes differed over "upright": some said the just, others that it is upright upon the Book of Allah and what He commanded. They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin good, forbid evil, and hasten to good deeds, racing in charity, and they are among the righteous, and Allah will not waste their reward. "The hours of the night" are the watches of the night when they stand in prayer reciting the Quran, and the exegetes differed: some said the depths of the night, others that it refers to those who prayed the last evening prayer. They prostrate and weep in their prayers, seeking the mercy of Allah. They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin the good, forbid the evil, and hasten to every good, racing one another in charity and obedience. Such are truly among the righteous, and Allah promises them the reward of the righteous, for He does not waste the reward of any doer of good, and He will admit them to His mercy on the Day of Judgment. The exegetes said that among the People of the Book there are those who combine all these qualities, and they will be rewarded according to their deeds, while the majority of them are rebellious, and the difference between them is clear to those who reflect.

phrases.ar: وَمَا يَفۡعَلُواْ مِنۡ خَيۡرٖ فَلَن يُكۡفَرُوهُۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِٱلۡمُتَّقِينَ
phrases.translation: They will never be denied the reward for any good they have done. And Allah has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of those mindful ˹of Him˺
phrases.explanation: "They will never be denied the reward for any good they have done. And Allah has perfect knowledge of those mindful of Him." "Whatever good they do": the reciters differed over the verb form, some reading it in the third person referring to the upright People of the Book, others in the second person. Either way, no good they do will be denied them or diminished, and Allah knows the God-fearing and will reward them fully, for He does not waste the reward of the doers of good. So do good and fear Allah, and He will reward you in full. And He knows the intentions of the God-fearing.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن تُغۡنِيَ عَنۡهُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلُهُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ شَيۡـٔٗاۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَصۡحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِۖ هُمۡ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
phrases.translation: Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah. It is they who will be the residents of the Fire. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, neither the wealth nor children of the disbelievers will be of any benefit to them against Allah. It is they who will be the residents of the Fire, abiding eternally therein." Those who disbelieve: their wealth and their children will not avail them anything against Allah on the Day of Judgment, for He does not accept ransom from the disbeliever. They are the companions of the Fire, abiding in it forever, and that is the recompense of disbelief after the truth came to them. Their wealth was spent in this life, and nothing of it will accompany them. Their end is the Fire, and no wealth can ransom them.

phrases.ar: مَثَلُ مَا يُنفِقُونَ فِي هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا كَمَثَلِ رِيحٖ فِيهَا صِرٌّ أَصَابَتۡ حَرۡثَ قَوۡمٖ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ فَأَهۡلَكَتۡهُۚ وَمَا ظَلَمَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَٰكِنۡ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
phrases.translation: The good they do in this worldly life is like the harvest of an evil people struck by a bitter wind, destroying it ˹completely˺. Allah never wronged them, but they wronged themselves
phrases.explanation: "The good they do in this worldly life is like the harvest of an evil people struck by a bitter wind, destroying it completely. Allah never wrongs people." The spending and good deeds of the disbelievers in this life are like a crop of a people struck by a freezing wind that destroys it entirely, so nothing of it avails them with Allah, for their deeds are not accepted because they disbelieved. Allah never wrongs people, but they wrong themselves by disbelief, and their deeds go to waste. So do not be like them, but spend in the cause of Allah while you are able. So seek the Hereafter with your deeds, for this life is deceptive.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ بِطَانَةٗ مِّن دُونِكُمۡ لَا يَأۡلُونَكُمۡ خَبَالٗا وَدُّواْ مَا عَنِتُّمۡ قَدۡ بَدَتِ ٱلۡبَغۡضَآءُ مِنۡ أَفۡوَٰهِهِمۡ وَمَا تُخۡفِي صُدُورُهُمۡ أَكۡبَرُۚ قَدۡ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِۖ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
phrases.translation: O believers! Do not associate closely with others who would not miss a chance to harm you. Their only desire is to see you suffer. Their prejudice has become evident from what they say—and what their hearts hide is far worse. We have made Our revelations clear to you, if only you understood
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Do not associate closely with others who would not miss a chance to harm you. Their only desire is to see you suffer. Their prejudice has become evident from their mouths, and what their hearts conceal is worse. Clear revelations have already come to you, if you understand." "Do not take as intimates": do not take a bosom friend from outside your faith, for their only wish is your affliction, and their hatred shows from their mouths while their hearts hide worse. The clear signs have come to you in the Quran, so understand and beware of them. Befriend only the believers, for they love you and wish you good.

phrases.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ أُوْلَآءِ تُحِبُّونَهُمۡ وَلَا يُحِبُّونَكُمۡ وَتُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡكِتَٰبِ كُلِّهِۦ وَإِذَا لَقُوكُمۡ قَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوۡاْ عَضُّواْ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡأَنَامِلَ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيۡظِۚ قُلۡ مُوتُواْ بِغَيۡظِكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
phrases.translation: Here you are! You love them but they do not love you, and you believe in all Scriptures. When they meet you they say, “We believe.” But when alone, they bite their fingertips in rage. Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “˹May you˺ die of your rage!” Surely Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart
phrases.explanation: "Here you are! You love them but they do not love you, and you believe in all the Scriptures. When they meet you they say: We believe. But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips out of rage at you. Say: Die in your rage, for Allah knows what is in the hearts." "Here you are": Allah addresses the believers who loved the hypocrites and People of the Book while they did not love them. You believe in all the books, but when they meet you they say "we believe," and when alone they bite their fingertips in rage against you. Say to them: perish in your rage, for Allah knows what is in the breasts, and He will requite the concealers of enmity. "The Book" here means the books, as the singular is used for the plural. The exegetes said this was revealed concerning the hypocrites of Medina, who showed faith outwardly while concealing disbelief, and their biting of the fingertips is a picture of their suppressed rage at the Muslims. Allah exposed their state in His Book so the believers would not be deceived by their claims of belief, and He knows what is in the hearts and will judge them for it. So do not take them as intimates, but treat them with caution, and Allah will protect you from their evil, for He knows their secret and their open. The believers are warned not to love them or trust them, for their love is not returned and their hearts hold rage, and only Allah knows the hearts truly.

phrases.ar: إِن تَمۡسَسۡكُمۡ حَسَنَةٞ تَسُؤۡهُمۡ وَإِن تُصِبۡكُمۡ سَيِّئَةٞ يَفۡرَحُواْ بِهَاۖ وَإِن تَصۡبِرُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ لَا يَضُرُّكُمۡ كَيۡدُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ مُحِيطٞ
phrases.translation: When you ˹believers˺ are touched with good, they grieve; but when you are afflicted with evil, they rejoice. ˹Yet,˺ if you are patient and mindful ˹of Allah˺, their schemes will not harm you in the least. Surely Allah is Fully Aware of what they do
phrases.explanation: "When you believers are touched with good, they grieve, but when you are afflicted with evil, they rejoice. Yet, if you are patient and mindful of Allah, their plotting will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah encompasses what they do." Their joy at your misfortune and grief at your good shows their enmity. But if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you in the least, for Allah surrounds what they do with knowledge, and He will requite them for it, and the patient God-fearing one is safe from their harm. So be patient and fear Allah, and their enmity will not avail them against you.

phrases.ar: وَإِذۡ غَدَوۡتَ مِنۡ أَهۡلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مَقَٰعِدَ لِلۡقِتَالِۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
phrases.translation: ˹Remember, O Prophet,˺ when you left your home in the early morning to position the believers in the battlefield. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing
phrases.explanation: "Remember, O Prophet, when you left your home in the early morning to position the believers in the battlefield. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." This refers to the day of Uhud, when the Prophet left his house early to arrange the believers in ranks for battle, and Allah heard and knew all, for He is All-Hearing of what is said and All-Knowing of what is concealed, and He aided His Prophet and the believers according to His wisdom. The positioning of the ranks was for the defense of Medina, and Allah knows the unseen and the seen. And He knows what the hearts conceal. He hears the supplication of the believers in battle.

phrases.ar: إِذۡ هَمَّت طَّآئِفَتَانِ مِنكُمۡ أَن تَفۡشَلَا وَٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُمَاۗ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when two groups among you ˹believers˺ were about to cower, then Allah reassured them. So in Allah let the believers put their trust
phrases.explanation: "Remember when two groups among you, believers, were about to cower, then Allah reassured them. So in Allah let the believers put their trust." Two groups of the believers, the sons of Salama and the sons of Kaab, were about to weaken and retreat at Uhud, but Allah strengthened them and reassured them, and He is their guardian and helper. So the believers should put their trust in Allah alone, for He is their protector and there is no victory except from Him. The two groups thought to retreat because of the intensity of the enemy, but Allah strengthened their hearts, and trust in Allah is the weapon of the believer in every battle. Whoever trusts Allah is never forsaken, and He suffices the believer. The guardian of the believers is Allah, and He never abandons them. When the believers saw the aid of Allah, their hearts were reassured.

phrases.ar: وَلَقَدۡ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِبَدۡرٖ وَأَنتُمۡ أَذِلَّةٞۖ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah made you victorious at Badr when you were ˹vastly˺ outnumbered. So be mindful of Allah, perhaps you will be grateful
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah made you victorious at Badr when you were vastly outnumbered. So be mindful of Allah, perhaps you will be grateful." Allah aided His Prophet and the believers at Badr, where the Muslims were few and poorly equipped and the enemy was many, and He made them victorious, for victory is from Allah alone. So be mindful of Allah and grateful for His favor, for gratitude is the means of increase, and the exegetes differed over why Badr was named Badr. The fewness of their number did not prevent the victory, for Allah is able to do all things. So remember the favor of Allah upon you at Badr.

phrases.ar: إِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَلَن يَكۡفِيَكُمۡ أَن يُمِدَّكُمۡ رَبُّكُم بِثَلَٰثَةِ ءَالَٰفٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ مُنزَلِينَ
phrases.translation: ˹Remember, O Prophet,˺ when you said to the believers, “Is it not enough that your Lord will send down a reinforcement of three thousand angels for your aid?”
phrases.explanation: "Remember, O Prophet, when you said to the believers: Is it not enough that your Lord will send down a reinforcement of three thousand angels?" At Badr the Prophet encouraged the believers, saying: is it not enough for you that your Lord will reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down. The exegetes differed over whether the angels came on that day, some saying they did not fight but their presence was promised, and others that Allah did send them and they fought. And the angels were promised to descend until the believers were reassured. The promise of Allah is true, and He does not break His promise.

phrases.ar: بَلَىٰٓۚ إِن تَصۡبِرُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ وَيَأۡتُوكُم مِّن فَوۡرِهِمۡ هَٰذَا يُمۡدِدۡكُمۡ رَبُّكُم بِخَمۡسَةِ ءَالَٰفٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ
phrases.translation: Most certainly, if you ˹believers˺ are firm and mindful ˹of Allah˺ and the enemy launches a sudden attack on you, Allah will reinforce you with five thousand angels designated ˹for battle˺
phrases.explanation: "Most certainly, if you believers are firm and mindful of Allah and the enemy launches a sudden attack on you, Allah will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels." If the believers are patient and God-fearing when the enemy attacks them suddenly, Allah will send five thousand angels marked with a sign, descending to aid them. The reciters differed over "marked": most read it as marked or distinguished, others as coming in succession. The promise is for those who hold firm, for Allah aids those who fear Him, and victory comes from Him alone. The marked angels came in ranks, wearing marks of wool, and they struck the enemy and turned them back. Hold firm then, and Allah will aid you as He aided the believers at Badr. The angels fought alongside the believers and struck fear into the enemy.

phrases.ar: وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشۡرَىٰ لَكُمۡ وَلِتَطۡمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُم بِهِۦۗ وَمَا ٱلنَّصۡرُ إِلَّا مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
phrases.translation: Allah ordained this ˹reinforcement˺ only as good news for you and reassurance for your hearts. And victory comes only from Allah—the Almighty, All-Wise—
phrases.explanation: "Allah ordained this reinforcement only as good news for you and reassurance for your hearts. And victory comes only from Allah, the Almighty, All-Wise." The sending of the angels was a glad tidings for the believers and a comfort to their hearts, that they would not be abandoned. And there is no victory except from Allah, the Almighty in His vengeance, the All-Wise in His management, for He gives victory to whom He wills, and the angels are only a means. So seek victory from Him alone and do not rely on numbers or equipment. So ask Him for victory and be grateful. So turn to Him in every affair and rely on Him alone.

phrases.ar: لِيَقۡطَعَ طَرَفٗا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَوۡ يَكۡبِتَهُمۡ فَيَنقَلِبُواْ خَآئِبِينَ
phrases.translation: to destroy a group of the disbelievers and humble the rest, causing them to withdraw in disappointment
phrases.explanation: "To destroy a group of the disbelievers and humble the rest, causing them to withdraw in disappointment." Allah aided the believers at Badr by cutting off a portion of the disbelievers, killing some and humbling the rest, so that they turned back disappointed with nothing gained. Some said the meaning is that there is no victory except from Allah, and He does with the disbelievers what He wills, cutting them off and humbling them, for He is the Almighty in His retribution upon whoever disobeys Him, the All-Wise in His management. The withdrawal in disappointment is the recompense of their disbelief and their flight from the truth.

phrases.ar: لَيۡسَ لَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءٌ أَوۡ يَتُوبَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ أَوۡ يُعَذِّبَهُمۡ فَإِنَّهُمۡ ظَٰلِمُونَ
phrases.translation: You ˹O Prophet˺ have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for indeed they are wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: "You, O Prophet, have no say in the matter. It is up to Allah to turn to them in mercy or punish them, for indeed they are wrongdoers." At Uhud the Prophet was wounded and some thought him killed, and the matter of the captives and the wounded was referred to Allah: "there is nothing for you in the affair," either He forgives them and turns to them in mercy, or He punishes them, for they are wrongdoers who disobeyed the Messenger. The grammar shows "turn to them" is coordinated with "punish them." So the Prophet has no share in the decision, and Allah decides as He wills.

phrases.ar: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ يَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورٞ رَّحِيمٞ
phrases.translation: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whoever He wills, and punishes whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful
phrases.explanation: "To Allah alone belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whoever He wills, and punishes whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful." Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, and He forgives whom He wills of His servants and punishes whom He wills according to His justice, for He is the Owner of all, doing what He wills. And He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful to those who repent and return to Him, so turn to Him and seek His forgiveness. His forgiveness and mercy are vast, and He accepts repentance from His servants until the sun rises from the west.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَأۡكُلُواْ ٱلرِّبَوٰٓاْ أَضۡعَٰفٗا مُّضَٰعَفَةٗۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
phrases.translation: O believers! Do not consume interest, multiplying it many times over. And be mindful of Allah, so you may prosper
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Do not consume interest, multiplying it many times over. And be mindful of Allah, so you may prosper." In the pre-Islamic era, a man would lend another a debt to a fixed term, and when the term came and the debtor could not pay, he would increase it and extend the term, doubling it again and again. Allah forbade this doubled, multiplied usury and commanded the believers to fear Him, for in abandoning usury is prosperity in this life and the next, and usury is a great sin that destroys wealth and society. So abandon usury and lend with the intention of helping your brother, seeking the pleasure of Allah.

phrases.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
phrases.translation: Guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: "Guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for the disbelievers." Fear the Fire that Allah has prepared for the disbelievers, and do good deeds that will save you from it, for the Fire is the severest punishment, prepared and blazing for those who disbelieve after the truth came to them. So guard yourselves by faith and obedience. It burns with the fuel of people and stones, and none will enter it except the disbelievers, and they will abide in it forever, so seek refuge in Allah from it. Guard yourselves by obeying Allah, doing good, and spending in His cause, for that is the protection from the Fire.

phrases.ar: وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
phrases.translation: Obey Allah and the Messenger, so you may be shown mercy
phrases.explanation: "Obey Allah and the Messenger, so you may be shown mercy." Obedience to Allah and His Messenger is the way to mercy and Paradise, for whoever obeys them is among the successful, and whoever disobeys them is among the losers. So obey Allah in what He commanded and avoid what He forbade, and follow the Messenger in his Sunna, so that Allah may have mercy on you. And whoever is shown mercy by Allah on that Day has attained the greatest success. So hasten to obedience and do not delay, for death may come suddenly. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has indeed found the straight path.

phrases.ar: ۞ وَسَارِعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةٖ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
phrases.translation: And hasten towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those mindful ˹of Allah˺
phrases.explanation: "And hasten towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as vast as the heavens and the earth, prepared for those mindful of Allah." Allah urges the believers to race toward His forgiveness and a Paradise whose width is like the heavens and the earth, as has been transmitted, prepared for the God-fearing who obey Him and avoid His prohibitions. So hasten to good deeds and repentance, for the Paradise is vast and Allah is generous to His servants, and the one who hastens to it attains it. The God-fearing are those who hasten to forgiveness and avoid sin. Race to it with righteous deeds and repentance.

phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ فِي ٱلسَّرَّآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَٱلۡكَٰظِمِينَ ٱلۡغَيۡظَ وَٱلۡعَافِينَ عَنِ ٱلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who donate in prosperity and adversity, control their anger, and pardon others. And Allah loves the good-doers
phrases.explanation: "They are those who donate in prosperity and adversity, control their anger, and pardon others. And Allah loves the good-doers." "In prosperity" means in ease and abundance of wealth, and "in adversity" in hardship and difficulty: they spend in charity in both states. "They control their anger": they restrain their rage and do not act on it. "And pardon people": they overlook the faults of others. Allah loves the doers of good, those who have these praiseworthy traits, and He will reward them. These traits are the best of character, and whoever has them is beloved to Allah. And hasten to pardon others, for pardoning is beloved to Allah.

phrases.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُواْ فَٰحِشَةً أَوۡ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ ذَكَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرُواْ لِذُنُوبِهِمۡ وَمَن يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَلَمۡ يُصِرُّواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُواْ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who, upon committing an evil deed or wronging themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness and do not knowingly persist in sin—and who forgives sins except Allah
phrases.explanation: "They are those who, upon committing an evil deed or wronging themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness and do not knowingly persist in sin. And there is no god but Allah, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful to His servants." When the believers commit a sin or wrong themselves, they remember Allah, seek His forgiveness for their sins, and do not persist in sin knowingly, for persistence in sin after knowledge is a great evil. "Indecency" refers to a grave sin. Allah is the Forgiver of sins, the Merciful to His servants, and He accepts their repentance, so hasten to repent before death. So do not despair of the mercy of Allah, whoever you are.

phrases.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ جَزَآؤُهُم مَّغۡفِرَةٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَجَنَّٰتٞ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَاۚ وَنِعۡمَ أَجۡرُ ٱلۡعَٰمِلِينَ
phrases.translation: Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens under which rivers flow, staying there forever. How excellent is the reward for those who work ˹righteousness˺
phrases.explanation: "Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens under which rivers flow, staying there forever. How excellent is the reward for those who do good." The reward of those who repent and do good is forgiveness from their Lord and Gardens of Paradise under which rivers flow, abiding in them forever. How excellent is the recompense of the doers of good, and that is the best reward, for Allah does not waste the reward of anyone who does good, and Paradise is the abode of the God-fearing. Paradise is the abode of bliss prepared by Allah for His believing servants. So strive for it with faith and good deeds.

phrases.ar: قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ سُنَنٞ فَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلۡمُكَذِّبِينَ
phrases.translation: Similar situations came to pass before you, so travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers
phrases.explanation: "Similar situations came to pass before you, so travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers." Many nations passed before you, O Muslims, who denied their prophets, so travel the earth and see the ruins of their dwellings and the fate of the deniers, how Allah destroyed them for their disbelief. The exegetes differed over which nations, but the lesson is that disbelief ends in destruction, and the believer should take warning. Take the lesson and do not follow their way, for whoever follows the deniers will meet their fate. The earth is full of their remains as a warning to the heedful. See how Allah dealt with them, and fear Him.

phrases.ar: هَٰذَا بَيَانٞ لِّلنَّاسِ وَهُدٗى وَمَوۡعِظَةٞ لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
phrases.translation: This is an insight to humanity—a guide and a lesson to the God-fearing
phrases.explanation: "This is an insight to humanity, a guide and a lesson to the God-fearing." "These are the ways of Allah": the stories of the past nations are a clear insight for mankind, a guidance and a lesson for those who fear Allah, so reflect upon them and take heed, and fear Allah lest His punishment seize you as it seized them. The stories of the past are narrated to you so that you may reflect, and the God-fearing are those who benefit from the lesson, so fear Allah and follow the guidance. Allah narrates the stories of the nations so that the believers may take lesson and the God-fearing may be guided, and the Quran is full of insight for those who reflect.

phrases.ar: وَلَا تَهِنُواْ وَلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَوۡنَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
phrases.translation: Do not falter or grieve, for you will have the upper hand, if you are ˹true˺ believers
phrases.explanation: "Do not falter or grieve, for you will have the upper hand, if you are true believers." Allah consoles the believers after Uhud: do not become weak because of what befell you, and do not grieve, for you are the uppermost, superior in religion and in the end, if you are believers. "Weak" comes from the saying of one who becomes weak in a matter, and the believers are commanded to hold firm, for Allah is with them and victory is theirs in the end. So be patient and do not despair, for Allah is with the patient. Hold firm upon your religion and Allah will aid you.

phrases.ar: إِن يَمۡسَسۡكُمۡ قَرۡحٞ فَقَدۡ مَسَّ ٱلۡقَوۡمَ قَرۡحٞ مِّثۡلُهُۥۚ وَتِلۡكَ ٱلۡأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنكُمۡ
phrases.translation: If you have suffered injuries ˹at Uḥud˺, they suffered similarly ˹at Badr˺. We alternate these days ˹of victory and defeat˺ among people so that Allah
phrases.explanation: "If you have suffered injuries at Uhud, they suffered similarly at Badr. We alternate these days of victory and defeat among people so that Allah may know the believers." If a wound afflicts you at Uhud, a similar wound afflicted the disbelievers at Badr. The reciters differed over the verb forms, but the meaning is clear: Allah alternates the days of victory and defeat among people, one group one day and another the next, so that He may know who the true believers are, those who hold firm in both states, and distinguish them from the hypocrites. The alternation of days is a sunna of Allah in His testing of His servants, that the believer is tried in victory and in defeat alike, and whoever is patient in both is among the true believers, for Allah loves the patient and He knows those who are sincere in their faith under all conditions. At Badr the believers were victorious and the disbelievers were struck, and at Uhud the reverse happened, and in each there is a lesson: that Allah tests His servants to distinguish the believer from the hypocrite, and whoever remains firm in faith in both ease and hardship is the true believer, and Allah knows the hearts. The days are given to one group and then to another, and this is the way of Allah with His prophets and their followers, that the truth may be manifest and the steadfastness of the believers known, for Allah is All-Knowing of who believes truly. This alternation is a mercy so that no people are destroyed utterly in one day, and a warning that the sunna of Allah is to test every nation.

phrases.ar: شُهَدَآءَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
phrases.translation: may reveal the ˹true˺ believers, choose martyrs from among you—and Allah does not like the wrongdoers—
phrases.explanation: "And distinguish the true believers and destroy the disbelievers." Allah purifies the believers through trials, testing their sincerity, and He blots out the disbelievers, diminishing and destroying them, for the trial separates the true from the false, and Allah knows those who strive and the patient. The purification of the believers and the destruction of the disbelievers are both from Allah, and He does what He wills with His creation. So do not let defeat discourage you, for Allah is with the believers. Allah purifies the believers by trials and removes the disbelievers little by little until they perish. And whoever remains firm in both states is the true believer.

phrases.ar: وَلِيُمَحِّصَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَيَمۡحَقَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
phrases.translation: and distinguish the ˹true˺ believers and destroy the disbelievers
phrases.explanation: "And distinguish the true believers and destroy the disbelievers." Allah tests the believers at Uhud to purify them and blot out the disbelievers, diminishing them and causing them to perish, for the trial reveals who is sincere and who is not, and Allah knows the strugglers and the patient among you. Purification comes through trial, and destruction is the end of the disbelievers, for Allah knows the true believers and will reward them. The trial at Uhud purified the believers and exposed the disbelievers, and Allah saw who stood firm. And He knows the patient among you, and He will reward them. So hold fast to faith in victory and defeat alike.

phrases.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَعۡلَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ جَٰهَدُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَيَعۡلَمَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
phrases.translation: Do you think you will enter Paradise without Allah proving which of you ˹truly˺ struggled ˹for His cause˺ and patiently endured
phrases.explanation: "Do you think you will enter Paradise without Allah proving which of you truly struggled for His cause and patiently endured?" Do you suppose, O believers, that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made known those who strove in His cause and those who were patient, for Paradise is not entered except by striving and patience. Allah knows the strugglers and the patient, and He will distinguish them on the Day of Judgment, rewarding each according to his deeds. So strive in His cause and endure with patience, and Allah will know you. Struggle and endure, and you will enter Paradise by the mercy of Allah.

phrases.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كُنتُمۡ تَمَنَّوۡنَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَلۡقَوۡهُ فَقَدۡ رَأَيۡتُمُوهُ وَأَنتُمۡ تَنظُرُونَ
phrases.translation: You certainly wished ˹for the opportunity˺ for martyrdom before encountering it, now you have seen it with your own eyes
phrases.explanation: "You certainly wished for the opportunity for martyrdom before encountering it, now you have seen it with your own eyes." You wished for death in the cause of Allah before you met it, and now at Uhud you saw it with your own eyes when the Prophet was reported killed. Some grammarians explained "while you were looking on" as emphasis. So do not wish for death now that you have seen its reality, but be patient and strive, for martyrdom is a great honor but not to be sought rashly. So be steadfast and do not turn back from striving. Death in the cause of Allah is a great honor, so do not flee from it when it comes.

phrases.ar: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٞ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُۚ أَفَإِيْن مَّاتَ أَوۡ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡقَٰبِكُمۡۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبۡ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيۡـٔٗاۚ وَسَيَجۡزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
phrases.translation: Muḥammad is no more than a messenger; other messengers have gone before him. If he were to die or to be killed, would you regress into disbelief? Those who do so will not harm Allah whatsoever. And Allah will reward those who are grateful
phrases.explanation: "Muhammad is no more than a messenger, other messengers have gone before him. If he were to die or be killed, would you regress into disbelief? Whoever regresses will not harm Allah at all. Allah will reward the grateful." Allah rebukes those who feared at Uhud that the Prophet was killed: Muhammad is only a messenger, and messengers before him died and were killed, so if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels to disbelief. Whoever turns back does not harm Allah anything, for the religion remains, and Allah will reward the grateful who hold firm upon Islam. So do not let the death of the messenger shake your faith, for Allah is ever-living and does not die.

phrases.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفۡسٍ أَن تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ كِتَٰبٗا مُّؤَجَّلٗاۗ وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَا وَمَن يُرِدۡ ثَوَابَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ نُؤۡتِهِۦ مِنۡهَاۚ وَسَنَجۡزِي ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
phrases.translation: No soul can ever die without Allah’s Will at the destined time. Those who desire worldly gain, We will let them have it, and those who desire heavenly reward, We will grant it to them. And We will reward those who are grateful
phrases.explanation: "No soul can ever die without Allah's Will at the destined time. Those who desire worldly gain, We will let them have it, and those who desire the reward of the Hereafter, We will give them of it. And Allah sees all that you do." No soul dies except by the permission of Allah at the appointed time written in the preserved tablet. Whoever seeks the gain of this world, Allah gives him of it, and whoever seeks the reward of the Hereafter, Allah gives him of it, for He is All-Seeing of what His servants do, and He recompenses each according to his intention, and nothing is hidden from Him. The destined time is written, and no soul can hasten or delay it. Whoever seeks the Hereafter will find it with Allah, for He is generous in reward. And do not be of those who prefer this world over the Hereafter.

phrases.ar: وَكَأَيِّن مِّن نَّبِيّٖ قَٰتَلَ مَعَهُۥ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٞ
phrases.translation: ˹Imagine˺ how many devotees fought along with their prophets and never faltered despite
phrases.explanation: "Imagine how many devotees fought along with their prophets and never faltered despite whatever losses they suffered in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken." "How many a prophet": the reciters differed over the reading, some with a hamza and doubling, others differently, but the meaning is "how many." With their prophets fought many bands of the believers, and they did not weaken or falter despite the losses and the killing of their prophet, for they knew that the prophets die and the religion remains. The reciters differed over "was killed": some read it passive, "the prophet was killed," meaning the prophet alone was killed and some of the devout ones, while others read it active, "fought," meaning they fought. "Devout throngs": the linguists differed over the word, some deriving it from the Lord, others saying it means the many throngs, their singular being a throng, and the exegetes differed likewise. Either way, the meaning is that many believers fought alongside their prophets through many trials, and when their prophet was slain they did not weaken or falter, but held fast to their religion, for they knew the messenger dies and the message remains. The lesson is that the believer does not despair when his leader is killed, for the prophets are but men, and the religion of Allah remains forever, and whoever holds fast to it is victorious in the end. They are an example for every generation, and their reward with Allah is great, for they bore the loss of their prophet with patience, and patience is the mark of the true believer, and Allah loves those who are patient in adversity. So when you hear that your leader has fallen, do not weaken, but know that Allah is with you.

phrases.ar: فَمَا وَهَنُواْ لِمَآ أَصَابَهُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا ضَعُفُواْ وَمَا ٱسۡتَكَانُواْۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
phrases.translation: whatever ˹losses˺ they suffered in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken or give in! Allah loves those who persevere
phrases.explanation: "Nor did they say, except: Our Lord, forgive our sins and our excesses in our affair, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter, for Allah loves the good-doers." Their saying was: our Lord, forgive us our sins, minor and major, and our going beyond the limit in the affair of battle, make our footsteps firm so we do not slip, and grant us victory over the disbelievers. So Allah answered them, gave them the victory and the reward of this world, and the excellent reward of the Hereafter, for Allah loves the doers of good who fight in His cause with patience.

phrases.ar: وَمَا كَانَ قَوۡلَهُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسۡرَافَنَا فِيٓ أَمۡرِنَا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
phrases.translation: And all they said was, “Our Lord! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people.”
phrases.explanation: "And all they said was: Our Lord! Forgive our sins and excesses, make our steps firm, and grant us victory over the disbelieving people." "Excess" means going beyond the limit. Their supplication combined seeking forgiveness for sins and excess, firmness in the battle, and victory over the enemy, and this is the supplication of the strugglers in the cause of Allah, asking Allah for forgiveness, steadfastness, and aid, for victory is from Allah alone. So make this your supplication in every battle, asking Allah for forgiveness, firmness, and victory. And Allah answers the supplication of the strugglers. Firmness in battle comes from Allah, and without Him there is no strength.

phrases.ar: فَـَٔاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ثَوَابَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَحُسۡنَ ثَوَابِ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
phrases.translation: So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. For Allah loves the good-doers
phrases.explanation: "So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. For Allah loves the good-doers." Allah gave those who fought with their prophet the reward of this world, the victory and the spoils, and the excellent reward of the Hereafter, the Gardens, for Allah loves the doers of good, those who fight in His cause with patience and sincerity, and He will not waste their reward. And whoever fights in His cause with patience will not be forsaken. So fight with patience and sincerity, seeking His pleasure. The good-doers are those who do good in secret and in public. And the Hereafter is better and more lasting.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِن تُطِيعُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَرُدُّوكُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَعۡقَٰبِكُمۡ فَتَنقَلِبُواْ خَٰسِرِينَ
phrases.translation: O believers! If you yield to the disbelievers, they will drag you back to disbelief—and you will become losers
phrases.explanation: "O believers! If you yield to the disbelievers, they will drag you back to disbelief, and you will become losers." Allah forbids the believers from obeying the disbelievers in their opinions and following their counsel in religion, for if you obey them, they will turn you back upon your heels to disbelief, and you will be losers in this life and the next. So hold fast to Islam and do not follow their way. So beware of their counsel and hold fast to your faith. The losers are those who turn back to disbelief. So do not yield to them in anything that contradicts your faith. Hold fast to the Quran and the Sunna.

phrases.ar: بَلِ ٱللَّهُ مَوۡلَىٰكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ خَيۡرُ ٱلنَّٰصِرِينَ
phrases.translation: But no! Allah is your Guardian, and He is the best Helper
phrases.explanation: "But no! Allah is your Guardian, and He is the best Helper." "Nay, Allah is your protector": your ally and helper against your enemies who disbelieve. "And He is the best of helpers": the best of those who aid, for His aid is complete and His victory is sure, so put your trust in Him alone, and whoever has Allah as guardian has no need of others. So call upon Him and rely on Him in every affair. He aids His party and humiliates His enemies. Call upon Him in hardship and in ease, and He will answer you. And He is the best of those who respond to the supplicant.

phrases.ar: سَنُلۡقِي فِي قُلُوبِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلرُّعۡبَ بِمَآ أَشۡرَكُواْ بِٱللَّهِ مَا لَمۡ يُنَزِّلۡ بِهِۦ سُلۡطَٰنٗاۖ وَمَأۡوَىٰهُمُ ٱلنَّارُۖ وَبِئۡسَ مَثۡوَى ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
phrases.translation: We will cast horror into the hearts of the disbelievers for associating ˹false gods˺ with Allah—a practice He has never authorized. The Fire will be their home—what an evil place for the wrongdoers to stay
phrases.explanation: "We will cast horror into the hearts of the disbelievers for associating false gods with Allah, a practice He has never authorized. The Fire will be their refuge, and what a miserable destination." Allah promises victory to the believers over their enemies at Uhud: He will cast fear into the hearts of the disbelievers because they associated partners with Allah without any authority or proof from Him. The Fire will be their abode on the Day of Judgment, and what an evil resting place it is, for they chose disbelief over faith and will abide in it forever. And the horror is because their hearts are empty of faith, so fear overcomes them when they face the believers.

phrases.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥٓ إِذۡ تَحُسُّونَهُم بِإِذۡنِهِۦۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا فَشِلۡتُمۡ وَتَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ وَعَصَيۡتُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَآ أَرَىٰكُم مَّا تُحِبُّونَۚ مِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرِيدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمۡ عَنۡهُمۡ لِيَبۡتَلِيَكُمۡۖ
phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you ˹initially˺ swept them away by His Will, then your courage weakened and you disputed about the command and disobeyed, after Allah had brought victory within your reach. Some of you were after worldly gain while others
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah fulfilled His promise to you when you initially swept them away by His Will, then your courage weakened and you disputed about the matter, and you disobeyed after He had shown you what you love. Among you are those who desire this world, and among you are those who desire the Hereafter." Allah fulfilled His promise to the believers at Uhud when they initially routed the enemy by His will, and the promise was the word of the Prophet to the archers to stay in their place. Then their courage weakened when they saw the spoils, and they disputed about dividing it, and disobeyed the command of the Messenger after Allah had shown them victory, which they loved. Among the believers are some who desire this worldly gain and some who desire the Hereafter, and Allah knows both and will reward each according to his intention. The archers left their posts to gather the spoils, which allowed the enemy to turn on you, and this was the cause of the reversal. Allah reminds you of this so that you would learn from it and not repeat it, for He is All-Knowing of what you conceal and what you reveal, and the desire for the world distracts from the Hereafter, so purify your intentions. Allah saw the state of your hearts, some firm and some weak, and He knows who among you truly desires the Hereafter, and He will give each his reward in full on the Day of Judgment. The promise of Allah is true, and He does not break His promise, so hold fast to it in every battle.

phrases.ar: وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا عَنكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو فَضۡلٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
phrases.translation: desired a heavenly reward. He denied you victory over them as a test, yet He has pardoned you. And Allah is Gracious to the believers
phrases.explanation: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in, until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. Nor would Allah inform you of the unseen, but Allah chooses a messenger from among you. And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful to you." Allah would not leave the believers in their present state of dispute and disobedience without distinguishing the wicked from the good, nor would He reveal the unseen to them, but He chooses a messenger to receive revelation. And He is All-Forgiving and Merciful to the believers who repent, for He forgave them their fleeing at Uhud when they returned to obedience. And He chose the Messenger to convey the revelation to you.

phrases.ar: ۞ إِذۡ تُصۡعِدُونَ وَلَا تَلۡوُۥنَ عَلَىٰٓ أَحَدٖ وَٱلرَّسُولُ يَدۡعُوكُمۡ فِيٓ أُخۡرَىٰكُمۡ
phrases.translation: ˹Remember˺ when you were running far away ˹in panic˺—not looking at anyone—while the Messenger was calling to you from behind! So Allah rewarded your disobedience
phrases.explanation: "Remember when you were running far away in panic, not looking at anyone, while the Messenger was calling to you from behind! So Allah rewarded you with distress upon distress." The reciters differed over the reading, but the meaning is: remember when you fled in panic at Uhud, turning your backs and not looking at anyone, while the Messenger called to you from behind, urging you to stand firm. So Allah recompensed you with one distress after another, the loss of victory and the wounding of the Prophet, so that you would not grieve over the spoils you lost, for the loss of the Hereafter is greater. The Messenger called them back to the ranks, but they did not hear because of the panic, and this is a lesson that the believer must obey the Messenger in battle as in peace, for obedience is the cause of victory, and disobedience is the cause of defeat, and Allah saw what you did. And the lesson remains for every generation: obey the Messenger and hold firm in the ranks, and Allah will aid you as He aided the believers at Badr. Allah rewards distress with distress so that you would turn away from the world, and He knows what is better for you than you know for yourselves.

phrases.ar: فَأَثَٰبَكُمۡ غَمَّۢا بِغَمّٖ لِّكَيۡلَا تَحۡزَنُواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمۡ وَلَا مَآ أَصَٰبَكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
phrases.translation: with distress upon distress. Now, do not grieve over the victory you were denied or the injury you suffered. And Allah is All-Aware of what you do
phrases.explanation: "So that you would not grieve over what you missed nor rejoice over what He gave you. Allah is All-Knowing of what you do." Allah recompensed the distress with distress so that the believers would not grieve over the worldly spoils they missed, nor rejoice excessively over what He gave them, for the worldly gain is temporary and the reward of the Hereafter is better and lasting. And Allah is All-Knowing of all your deeds, and He will requite you for them, so do good and do not let the world distract you from the Hereafter. So be grateful for what He gave you and patient over what you missed, for the reward of Allah is better than the spoils of this world. So do not let the love of the world overcome your love of Allah.

phrases.ar: ثُمَّ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡغَمِّ أَمَنَةٗ نُّعَاسٗا يَغۡشَىٰ طَآئِفَةٗ مِّنكُمۡۖ وَطَآئِفَةٞ قَدۡ أَهَمَّتۡهُمۡ أَنفُسُهُمۡ يَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡحَقِّ ظَنَّ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِۖ يَقُولُونَ هَل لَّنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِن شَيۡءٖۗ قُلۡ إِنَّ ٱلۡأَمۡرَ كُلَّهُۥ لِلَّهِۗ يُخۡفُونَ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِم مَّا لَا يُبۡدُونَ لَكَۖ يَقُولُونَ لَوۡ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ ٱلۡأَمۡرِ شَيۡءٞ مَّا قُتِلۡنَا هَٰهُنَاۗ
phrases.translation: Then after distress, He sent down serenity in the form of drowsiness overcoming some of you, while others were disturbed by evil thoughts about Allah—the thoughts of ˹pre-Islamic˺ ignorance. They ask, “Do we have a say in the matter?” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “All matters are destined by Allah.” They conceal in their hearts what they do not reveal to you. They say ˹to themselves˺, “If we had any say in the matter, none of us would have come to die
phrases.explanation: "Then after distress, He sent down serenity in the form of drowsiness overcoming some of you, while others were disturbed by evil thoughts about Allah, saying in the time of ignorance: What concern do we have in this affair? Say, O Prophet: The affair belongs entirely to Allah. They hide in their hearts what they do not reveal to you. They say: If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here. Say: Even if you were in your homes, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their place of death. And that Allah may test what is in your hearts and purify what is in your hearts. Allah is All-Knowing of what is in the hearts." After the distress at Uhud, Allah sent down security in the form of a drowsiness that overcame a group of the believers, while another group was preoccupied with themselves, thinking selfishly and saying, as in the days of ignorance, "what concern do we have in this affair." So the Prophet is told: the whole affair belongs to Allah alone, and they hide in their hearts enmity and hypocrisy that they do not show. They say: if we had any say, we would not have been killed here. Say: even if you had stayed in your homes, those decreed to be killed would have gone out to the place of their death, for death comes at its appointed time. And all this was so that Allah might test what is in your breasts and purify your hearts, for Allah knows what is in the hearts, and He forgave those who repented. The drowsiness that overcame the believers was a calm from Allah that settled their hearts after the panic, while the other group were the hypocrites, concerned only with themselves.

phrases.ar: قُل لَّوۡ كُنتُمۡ فِي بُيُوتِكُمۡ لَبَرَزَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلۡقَتۡلُ إِلَىٰ مَضَاجِعِهِمۡۖ وَلِيَبۡتَلِيَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمۡ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
phrases.translation: here.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Even if you were to remain in your homes, those among you who were destined to be killed would have met the same fate.” Through this, Allah tests what is within you and purifies what is in your hearts. And Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those who fled on the day when the two armies met were made to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds. But Allah has pardoned them. Allah is indeed Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful." Those who turned away at Uhud were made to slip by Satan because of their sins, namely leaving their posts for the spoils, but Allah pardoned them, for He is Oft-Forgiving and Merciful, and He accepts the repentance of those who return to Him. And the lesson is that death cannot be avoided by staying home, for the soul goes forth to its decreed place, and the believer should not fear death in the cause of Allah, while the hypocrite fears it and wishes to flee, and Allah knows the difference between them and will requite each accordingly. And do not fear death when it comes in the cause of Allah. And whoever fears Allah in secret and in public is among the forgiven.

phrases.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوۡاْ مِنكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ إِنَّمَا ٱسۡتَزَلَّهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بِبَعۡضِ مَا كَسَبُواْۖ وَلَقَدۡ عَفَا ٱللَّهُ عَنۡهُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٞ
phrases.translation: Indeed, those ˹believers˺ who fled on the day when the two armies met were made to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds. But Allah has pardoned them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, those believers who fled on the day when the two armies met were made to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds. But Allah has pardoned them. Allah is indeed Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful." "Turned away" is from turning the back. Those who fled at Uhud were caused to slip by Satan because of their misdeeds, but Allah forgave them, for He is Oft-Forgiving and Most Merciful, and He accepts the repentance of those who return to Him, so do not despair of His mercy. Their slip was because they loved the spoils more than obedience, and Satan made that appear good to them, but Allah is Oft-Forgiving to those who repent and return, so do not persist in sin, and ask Allah for forgiveness in every battle. Repent and do not return to it.

phrases.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَقَالُواْ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمۡ إِذَا ضَرَبُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أَوۡ كَانُواْ غُزّٗى لَّوۡ كَانُواْ عِندَنَا مَا مَاتُواْ وَمَا قُتِلُواْ لِيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ حَسۡرَةٗ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡۗ
phrases.translation: O believers! Do not be like the unfaithful who say about their brothers who travel throughout the land or engage in battle, “If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed.” Allah makes such thinking a cause of agony in
phrases.explanation: "O believers! Do not be like the unfaithful who say about their brothers who travel throughout the land or engage in battle: If they had stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed. Say: Would you ward off death from yourselves if you were to die? Allah is the One who gives life and causes death. And He is All-Aware of what is in the hearts." The believers are forbidden to imitate the disbelievers who say that about their dead brothers, for death is decreed and cannot be averted by staying home. Say to them: if you could ward off death, death would not have come to you when it did. Allah alone gives life and causes death, and He knows what is in the hearts, so fear Him. It has been said that this was revealed concerning those who said at Uhud that if their brothers had stayed they would not have been killed, and the answer is that death is decreed, and no one can escape it, so do not grieve excessively for the dead, but remember them and ask forgiveness for them, and be patient, for Allah is with the patient, and He knows what is in the hearts of the truthful and the liars. Grieve not for them, but ask Allah to forgive them and have mercy on them.

phrases.ar: وَٱللَّهُ يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٞ
phrases.translation: their hearts. It is Allah who gives life and causes death. And Allah is All-Seeing of what you do
phrases.explanation: "Say: Would you ward off death from yourselves if you were to die? Allah is the One who gives life and causes death. And He is All-Aware of what is in the hearts." This is the answer to their claim: you cannot prevent death, for Allah is the giver of life and the causer of death, at the appointed time and place, and He is aware of all that is in the hearts, so do not speak of what you do not know, and fear the One who owns the souls. So turn to Him and do not say what you do not know. And rely on Him alone.

phrases.ar: وَلَئِن قُتِلۡتُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡ مُتُّمۡ لَمَغۡفِرَةٞ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَحۡمَةٌ خَيۡرٞ مِّمَّا يَجۡمَعُونَ
phrases.translation: Should you be martyred or die in the cause of Allah, then His forgiveness and mercy are far better than whatever ˹wealth˺ those ˹who stay behind˺ accumulate
phrases.explanation: "Should you be martyred or die in the cause of Allah, then His forgiveness and mercy are far better than whatever wealth those who stayed behind accumulate." If you are killed in the way of Allah or die upon Islam, then the forgiveness of Allah and His mercy are better for you than all the wealth that those who stayed behind from the battle gather, for martyrdom and dying upon faith are the greatest gain, and the worldly spoils are temporary and perishing. So do not grieve over missing the spoils, and strive in the cause of Allah. And the martyrs are not dead, but alive with their Lord, provisioned.

phrases.ar: وَلَئِن مُّتُّمۡ أَوۡ قُتِلۡتُمۡ لَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
phrases.translation: Whether you die or are martyred—all of you will be gathered before Allah
phrases.explanation: "Whether you die or are martyred, all of you will be gathered before Allah." If you die or are killed, you will be resurrected and gathered to Allah on the Day of Judgment, where He will judge between His servants, so death is not the end, and the martyr is alive with his Lord. So fear Allah and do not prefer this world over the Hereafter. So prepare for that meeting by obeying Allah and His Messenger in this life. And He will recompense every soul for what it earned. So do not grieve over death, for it is a meeting with Allah. And the believer does not fear death, for it is a door to Paradise.

phrases.ar: فَبِمَا رَحۡمَةٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلۡقَلۡبِ لَٱنفَضُّواْ مِنۡ حَوۡلِكَۖ
phrases.translation: It is out of Allah’s mercy that you ˹O Prophet˺ have been lenient with them. Had you been cruel or hard-hearted, they would have certainly abandoned you. So pardon them, ask
phrases.explanation: "It is out of Allah's mercy that you, O Prophet, have been lenient with them. Had you been cruel or hard-hearted, they would have certainly dispersed from around you. So pardon them and ask Allah's forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter." Allah says to His Prophet: it is by His mercy that you dealt gently with the believers after Uhud, for had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from you. So pardon them, seek forgiveness for them from Allah, and consult them in the affairs, for consultation softens hearts and unites them, and the Prophet consulted his companions at Uhud. So be lenient with the believers and overlook their faults.

phrases.ar: فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمۡتَ فَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
phrases.translation: Allah’s forgiveness for them, and consult with them in ˹conducting˺ matters. Once you make a decision, put your trust in Allah. Surely Allah loves those who trust in Him
phrases.explanation: "And when you have decided, then put your trust in Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who put their trust in Him." When you have resolved upon a matter after consulting them, then rely on Allah alone, for He suffices you, and whoever trusts Allah is guided and aided. And Allah loves the tawakkul, those who put their trust in Him after doing their part, for He is their guardian and helper, and there is no strength except with Him. Trust in Allah is the refuge of the believer in every affair, great or small, and whoever does so will never be forsaken, for Allah is with those who trust in Him. The believers are brothers, and love for them is part of faith. He is the best of trustees, and He suffices the believer in every matter. Consult the believers in your affairs, and trust Allah when you decide.

phrases.ar: إِن يَنصُرۡكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمۡۖ وَإِن يَخۡذُلۡكُمۡ فَمَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَنصُرُكُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۗ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلۡيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
phrases.translation: If Allah helps you, none can defeat you. But if He denies you help, then who else can help you? So in Allah let the believers put their trust
phrases.explanation: "If Allah helps you, none can defeat you. But if He denies you help, then who else can help you? So in Allah let the believers put their trust." Allah says: if He aids you, no one can overcome you, for His aid is with His party. But if He forsakes you, then who can aid you besides Him, for all helpers are in His hand. So the believers should put their trust in Allah alone, for He is their helper and guardian, and whoever He aids is victorious, and whoever He forsakes is forsaken. So call upon Him and rely on Him in hardship and in ease.

phrases.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَن يَغُلَّۚ وَمَن يَغۡلُلۡ يَأۡتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۚ
phrases.translation: It is not appropriate for a prophet to illegally withhold spoils of war. And whoever does so, it will be held against them on the Day
phrases.explanation: "It is not appropriate for a prophet to illegally withhold spoils of war. And whoever does so, it will be held against them on the Day of Judgment." The reciters differed over the reading: some read it as "it does not befit a prophet to be unfaithful," meaning to embezzle the spoils, and the verse was revealed concerning the spoils at Uhud when some took a portion. "Whoever embezzles": whoever takes from the spoils unlawfully, it will be brought against him on the Day of Judgment, and he will be recompensed for it, for Allah is severe in punishment, and the spoils must be divided justly among all. The exegetes said this was revealed when a red cloak from the spoils went missing, and the Prophet was accused of taking it, so Allah cleared him and forbade embezzlement for any prophet, for the prophets are the most truthful and the least likely to betray a trust. The spoils of war belong to all the fighters and must be divided fairly, and whoever withholds any of it will have it brought against him on the Day of Judgment as a fire that he will carry, and Allah will requite him for it, for He is All-Seeing of what His servants do. Others read it as: it does not befit a prophet that his companions be unfaithful to him, and others that he should be accused of treachery, so the verse clears the prophet of any such accusation and forbids treachery in general, whether by the prophet or by the companions, for the spoils are a trust, and the community must guard them and divide them justly. The majority reading forbids the prophet himself from embezzlement, and the verse came to clear him of the accusation, for he is the most truthful of people and the guardian of the trust, and Allah protected him from any suspicion, so that the believers would trust him fully and the spoils would be divided with justice, for injustice in the spoils breeds enmity among the fighters.

phrases.ar: ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ مَّا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
phrases.translation: of Judgment. Then every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and none will be wronged
phrases.explanation: "Are those who seek Allah's pleasure like those who deserve Allah's wrath? Hell is their home. What an evil destination!" Is the one who follows the pleasure of Allah, by obeying Him and not embezzling the spoils, like the one who incurs His anger by disobeying and embezzling. Hell is the abode of the latter, and what an evil resting place, for he chose the wrath of Allah over His pleasure, and he will abide in the Fire forever. So seek the pleasure of Allah by obedience and justice. And whoever avoids the wrath of Allah attains His pleasure. So obey and be just. And whoever fears Allah will attain the pleasure of Allah.

phrases.ar: أَفَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ رِضۡوَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ كَمَنۢ بَآءَ بِسَخَطٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَأۡوَىٰهُ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
phrases.translation: Are those who seek Allah’s pleasure like those who deserve Allah’s wrath? Hell is their home. What an evil destination
phrases.explanation: "Are those who seek Allah's pleasure like those who deserve Allah's wrath? Hell is their home. What an evil destination!" Some said this refers to the one who embezzled the spoils and incurred the anger of Allah, and others to every disbeliever. Either way, the one who seeks the pleasure of Allah by obedience is not like the one who brings upon himself His wrath by disobedience. Hell is the home of the latter, and what an evil destination it is, so seek the pleasure of Allah and avoid His wrath. And the pleasure of Allah is Paradise, the best destination. So hasten to obedience and avoid disobedience. And Paradise is better than the Fire. So strive for the pleasure of Allah in all your deeds.

phrases.ar: هُمۡ دَرَجَٰتٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ بَصِيرُۢ بِمَا يَعۡمَلُونَ
phrases.translation: They ˹each˺ have varying degrees in the sight of Allah. And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do
phrases.explanation: "They each have varying degrees in the sight of Allah. And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do." The believers are not equal in rank before Allah: some have higher degrees than others according to their faith and deeds, and the one who seeks His pleasure has high ranks with Him. And Allah sees all that they do, and He will requite each according to his deeds, so strive for the higher degrees by obedience and good deeds. So compete in good deeds to raise your degree. And do not be envious of one another, for Allah gives His bounty to whom He wills. And He is All-Knowing of the doers of good.

phrases.ar: لَقَدۡ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ إِذۡ بَعَثَ فِيهِمۡ رَسُولٗا مِّنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡ يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلُ لَفِي ضَلَٰلٖ مُّبِينٍ
phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah has done the believers a ˹great˺ favour by raising a messenger from among them—reciting to them His revelations, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom. For indeed they had previously been clearly astray
phrases.explanation: "Indeed, Allah has done the believers a great favour by raising a messenger from among them, reciting to them His revelations, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom. Before that you were clearly astray." Allah favored the believers by sending a messenger from among themselves, of their own lineage and language, who recites the Quran to them, purifies them from polytheism and sin, and teaches them the Book and wisdom. Before that they were in clear error, upon disbelief and ignorance, so this is among the greatest favors of Allah, and be grateful for it by obeying the Messenger. And follow him in all he brought, for he came with the truth.

phrases.ar: أَوَلَمَّآ أَصَٰبَتۡكُم مُّصِيبَةٞ قَدۡ أَصَبۡتُم مِّثۡلَيۡهَا قُلۡتُمۡ أَنَّىٰ هَٰذَاۖ قُلۡ هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ أَنفُسِكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ
phrases.translation: Why is it when you suffered casualties ˹at Uḥud˺—although you had made your enemy suffer twice as much ˹at Badr˺—you protested, “How could this be?”? Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “It is because of your disobedience.” Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: "Why is it that when you suffered casualties at Uhud, although you had made your enemy suffer twice as much at Badr, you protested: How could this happen to us? Say: It comes from yourselves. Allah is Almighty, All-Wise." When the calamity of Uhud befell you, though you had inflicted twice upon the enemy at Badr, you said: how did this happen to us. Say, O Muhammad: it is from yourselves, because of the disobedience of the archers who left their posts. The exegetes differed over the details, but Allah is Almighty in His decree and All-Wise in His legislation, and what befalls you is by His permission, as a test and a reminder, so be patient and accept the decree of Allah.

phrases.ar: وَمَآ أَصَٰبَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
phrases.translation: So what you suffered on the day the two armies met was by Allah’s Will, so that He might distinguish the ˹true˺ believers
phrases.explanation: "So what you suffered on the day the two armies met was by Allah's Will, so that He might distinguish the true believers and expose the hypocrites." What afflicted you at Uhud was by the permission of Allah, for nothing happens except by His will, and He permitted it so that He might know the true believers, those who held firm, and expose the hypocrites, those who fled and showed their hypocrisy. So the trial separates the sincere from the false, and Allah knows what is in the hearts. So hold fast to faith in victory and defeat alike. And do not let the trial shake your faith.

phrases.ar: وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَافَقُواْۚ وَقِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ قَٰتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوِ ٱدۡفَعُواْۖ قَالُواْ لَوۡ نَعۡلَمُ قِتَالٗا لَّٱتَّبَعۡنَٰكُمۡۗ هُمۡ لِلۡكُفۡرِ يَوۡمَئِذٍ أَقۡرَبُ مِنۡهُمۡ لِلۡإِيمَٰنِۚ يَقُولُونَ بِأَفۡوَٰهِهِم مَّا لَيۡسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَكۡتُمُونَ
phrases.translation: and expose the hypocrites. When it was said to them, “Come fight in the cause of Allah or ˹at least˺ defend yourselves,” they replied, “If we had known there was fighting, we would have definitely gone with you.” They were closer to disbelief than to belief on that day—for saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. Allah is All-Knowing of what they hide
phrases.explanation: "And expose the hypocrites. When it was said to them: Come, fight in the cause of Allah or at least defend yourselves, they replied: If we knew how to fight, we would have followed you. On that day they were closer to disbelief than to faith, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. Say: Allah knows what you conceal better than you know it yourselves." "Or defend": some said it means increase your numbers, for numbers repel the enemy. The hypocrites refused, and they were closer to disbelief than to faith. Say: Allah knows what you conceal better than you know yourselves. And fear Allah, for He sees your hypocrisy.

phrases.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمۡ وَقَعَدُواْ لَوۡ أَطَاعُونَا مَا قُتِلُواْۗ قُلۡ فَٱدۡرَءُواْ عَنۡ أَنفُسِكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
phrases.translation: Those who sat at home, saying about their brothers, “Had they listened to us, they would not have been killed.” Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Try not to die if what you say is true!”
phrases.explanation: "Those who sat at home, saying about their brothers: Had they listened to us, they would not have been killed. Say, O Prophet: Try to avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful." Allah reports the saying of those who stayed home at Uhud, who said about their slain brothers: if they had obeyed us and stayed, they would not have been killed. So the Prophet is told to answer them: try to ward off death from yourselves, if you are truthful in your claim, for death comes at its decreed time and cannot be averted by staying home. And they said this out of cowardice, and Allah knows their hearts.

phrases.ar: وَلَا تَحۡسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ قُتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَمۡوَٰتَۢاۚ بَلۡ أَحۡيَآءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ يُرۡزَقُونَ
phrases.translation: Never think of those martyred in the cause of Allah as dead. In fact, they are alive with their Lord, well provided for—
phrases.explanation: "Never think of those martyred in the cause of Allah as dead. In fact, they are alive with their Lord, well provided for, rejoicing in Allah's bounties and being delighted for those yet to join them. There will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve." Those killed in the way of Allah, such as the martyrs of Uhud, are not dead but alive with Allah, enjoying His provision in Paradise, rejoicing in His bounty and glad for their brothers who will join them in martyrdom, for there is no fear for them nor grief. So do not think of them as dead, but ask Allah to join you to them.

phrases.ar: فَرِحِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَيَسۡتَبۡشِرُونَ بِٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَلۡحَقُواْ بِهِم مِّنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ أَلَّا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
phrases.translation: rejoicing in Allah’s bounties and being delighted for those yet to join them. There will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve
phrases.explanation: "They are joyful for receiving Allah's grace and bounty, and that Allah does not deny the reward of the believers."
